thread:
maria_p: Heads-up — prod tenant t-09b hit intermittent throttling during a dedicated pool warmup. Apps got 429s for ~3m starting ~2026-03-15T10:05Z. Posting logs I grabbed.

alex.k: Which pool and exact window? Any recent config changes or plan migrations for t-09b?

maria_p: pool dp-42, window ~10:05:12 -> 10:08:30 UTC. They moved from free-tier->reserved yesterday (plan change) but traffic pattern is normal.

maria_p: Logs excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] WARN tenant=t-09b pool=dp-42 code=429 msg="rate_limited" quota_remaining=0 window_ms=60000
[2026-03-15T10:05:30Z] INFO tenant=t-09b bucket_state="tokens=-5" refill_rate=1/s capacity=100 burst=100
[2026-03-15T10:06:02Z] WARN tenant=t-09b code=429 msg="rate_limited" tokens=-12
[2026-03-15T10:08:31Z] INFO tenant=t-09b code=200 msg="request_ok" tokens=37
```

jordan_r: SRE alert fired too: sre_bot posted a DedicatedPoolThrottle alert at 10:05:15. Refs: <https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/DP-THROTTLE-307>

sre_bot: Alert: DedicatedPoolThrottle(dp-42) tenants=[t-09b] 429-rate > 5% in 1m. Autoscale event started at 10:04:50 UTC. :warning:

alex.k: Two hypotheses: 1) per-tenant rate config didn't apply correctly after migration, or 2) warmup/autoscale path temporarily turns off burst tokens. Can infra run a quota/view on that tenant in the pool?

support_lead: Please run the internal inspector: `quota-inspect --tenant t-09b --pool dp-42 --since 2026-03-15T09:55Z` and paste output.

infra_eng: Ran it. Output below (sanitized):
```
quota-config: tenant=t-09b pool=dp-42 rate_unit=hour limit=3600 burst=100
runtime-limiter: interprets rate_unit=minute (legacy) -> effective_limit=3600/minute
token-bucket: capacity=100 refill=1/s
recent-usage: 2200 reqs in window 10:00-10:06
```

infra_eng: TL;DR — config upload used units=hour but the runtime expects minute (old/legacy enum). That makes the tenant effectively allowed 3600 requests per minute instead of per hour, which then interacts badly with burst math (we see tokens underflowing). There's a conversion bug in the policy-migration codepath that maps new plan uploads to runtime format.

maria_p: So runtime treated 3600/hour as 3600/min? That would explain sudden immediate denial during warmup. But why negative tokens? Shouldn't bucket just cap at 0?

infra_eng: The negative tokens come from a short window where the refill/settle logic runs with different denominators between the policy applier and the runtime cache — race + unit mismatch. We've reproduced locally with a unit conversion test. Repro steps:
```
1) apply policy: limit=3600 unit=hour
2) simulate burst of 2k reqs in 30s
3) observe token_bucket.tokens go negative for 2-3s
```

support_lead: Immediate mitigation options — (A) bump burst for t-09b to large value until hotfix deployed, (B) temporarily route t-09b to quiet pool with looser limits, (C) rollback the recent plan migration for the tenant. Which is lowest blast radius?

alex.k: (A) is lowest impact and fastest: `quota-set --tenant t-09b --pool dp-42 --burst 1000` — do that now while infra prepares hotfix. Also add a temporary rate-limit override so requests don't get negative token handling.

infra_eng: Applying (A) now.

infra_eng: Patch command executed: `quota-set --tenant t-09b --pool dp-42 --burst 1000 --reason "hotfix warmup throttle"` -> applied at 2026-03-15T10:11:03Z. Also pushed a quick runtime guard to clamp tokens>=0 until full fix.

sre_bot: Alert update: DedicatedPoolThrottle(dp-42) reduced to 0.8% in 1m after mitigation. :good:

maria_p: Confirming from app logs — 429s stopped after ~10:11:10. Thanks.

infra_eng: Root cause: plan-migration job wrote rate_unit as "hour" but runtime mapper expected legacy enum (minutes). Fix in PR: https://repo.redwood.internal/infra/pull/5421 — adds explicit unit translation and unit tests. Hotfix also clamps tokens in runtime and emits a migration-time warning for mismatched enums.

support_lead: Action items:
- infra_eng: merge + deploy PR 5421 (owner) — deploy by EOD 2026-03-15
- infra_eng: add migration validation test in migration pipeline (owner) — due 2026-03-18
- platform: add a runbook note and automated post-migration check (owner: support_lead) — due 2026-03-17

alex.k: Also adding an integration test to simulate warmup+policy-change (jordan_r to own). 

jordan_r: I'll create the test and link it here. :thumbsup:

maria_p: Thanks team — keeping t-09b on monitor for 24h and will update if anything else shows up.

infra_eng: Patch merged and deployed at 2026-03-15T16:42Z. Verified migration job now emits an error if units unknown. No further 429s for t-09b during additional stress tests.

support_lead: Closing thread when we have runbook PR and test in main. Good job everyone. :clap:
